ships.rebuild_of: ship 002 attempt 1 (2026-08-02, checker FAIL x2 on a hand-rolled glob->RegExp compiler). Semantics BORROWED from nektos/act pkg/workflowpattern (MIT, commit 4f411281417e88660bea1c1a1749aa71ae0bd60f); execution deliberately NOT ported, because act is linear-time only by virtue of Go's RE2 and a verbatim JS port would have reintroduced the same ReDoS.
ships.checker_verdict: PASS after one fix cycle. THREE independent checkers, none given a prior verdict, all on a DIFFERENT MODEL from the maker. PASS 1 primary, verbatim: "VERDICT: PARTIAL - matcher is correct (0/56,766 divergences, 46/46, 64/64, 14/14 e2e), secure (0 XSS, no proto-pollution), private (1 request, 0 cookies/storage), and premises are docs-accurate, but the page's absolute printed claim 'No input can make it hang' is false: a pasteable pattern/value pair produces a measured 5.6 s synchronous tab freeze because the linear-time Pike VM is still O(pattern x value) with no input-size guard." PASS 1 independent security adversary, verbatim: "VERDICT: FAIL - the freeze/hang objective produced multiple reproduced, measured defects (up to a full tab crash and multi-ten-second blocks well past the claimed 50ms ceiling), directly falsifying 'No input can make it hang,' while the XSS objective found nothing across an exhaustive, corpus-plus-hundreds-more sweep." It measured 7,755 ms on 5,000 files x 100 patterns (proven a true event-loop freeze: a screenshot 300 ms in timed out without returning a frame, and a 5 ms interval canary ticked 3 times where ~1,358 were due), 12,889 ms on 2,000-level nested YAML with no glob patterns at all, >90 s unfinished on '*?'x20000, and a TAB CRASH on a 20,000-level document. FIX CYCLE (one, as the contract allows): a work budget decremented by NFA states actually visited and checked inside the loop - unlike ship 002's failed static budget it measures work already done rather than predicting an exponential blow-up, so it cannot be satisfied and exceeded at once; out of budget yields CANNOT TELL, never a verdict. Plus encode-each-value-once, cached NFA scratch state, 1 MiB / 20k-line / 64-level parser limits, textLength checked before .value, clear-before-compute, 5,000-file and 4,096-char field caps, and the printed claim narrowed to what was actually proven. TARGETED RE-CHECK by a fresh adversary on the fix diff, verbatim: "VERDICT: PASS - every reported defect is fixed and neither the cached NFA scratch state nor the shared work budget produced any wrong verdict across ~69.5k RE2-differential and 6.1k bounded-vs-unbounded comparisons; the only residuals are two low-severity, sub-second UX/copy nuances." Before/after it measured: 7,755 ms -> 150 ms; 5,618 ms -> 188 ms; 9,675 ms -> 238 ms; >90 s -> 194 ms; 12.9 s / tab crash -> refused in 0 ms with no crash; 4,578 ms -> 0.9 ms. TWO RESIDUALS CARRIED, NOT FIXED (recorded rather than ground down - the contract allows one fix cycle, and changing code after the verdict would mean staging something unverified): (1) LOW stale-verdict-repaint - run() is synchronous so the clear() at its top is never painted before the compute, leaving the previous verdict as the last painted frame for up to ~0.67 s; DOM state is correct and a MutationObserver confirmed the old verdict is never re-inserted as current. (2) LOW copy-latency-scope - the copy's 'about a fifth of a second' is scoped to matching work and matches the measured ~0.23 s budget, but pattern compilation and YAML parsing sit outside the budget, so worst-case total latency is ~667 ms, roughly 3x what a reader may infer. VERIFIED SOUND across the round: 211,118 (pattern,value) pairs by the maker plus 56,766 and ~69,500 by two checkers against their OWN Go/RE2 builds of act, ZERO divergences in every set; 203,082 reuse comparisons proving the cached scratch state never changes an answer; 6,144 bounded-vs-unbounded comparisons proving the budget only ever declines, never flips a verdict; GitHub's published cheat sheet 46/46 and act's own corpus 64/64 run against the LIVE page; 5 GitHub filter premises re-verified against docs.github.com; ~870 XSS payloads across every field including the thrown-Error sink, 0 injections, 0 prototype pollution; no new RegExp on user input, sole innerHTML assignment is a static ''; every stated limit off-by-one correct and named in its refusal message; 1 external request (the cookieless Cloudflare beacon), 0 cookies, 0 storage. Live-URL unverified by this run (egress; no desktop bridge in a scheduled run) - and health.json does not exist because .github/workflows/ has not been added to the repo.

ships.one_liner: paste a CODEOWNERS file and the paths a PR touches — get the rule that wins per file, the owners requested, the rules that lost, and the lines GitHub silently skips
ships.gap_source_url: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners — EVERGREEN lane, why-now waived; the permanent demand is GitHub's own counter-intuitive precedence rule ("Order is important; the last matching pattern takes the most precedence") plus three documented footguns (! negation, [ ] ranges and \# escaping all silently do nothing) and silent line-skipping on any syntax error. Occupant hunt 2026-08-04, named and all CLI/library-shaped: hmarr/codeowners (Go CLI+lib), mszostok/codeowners-validator, orsinium-labs/owners, topfreegames/codeowners-verifier, nmusolino/codeowners, multimediallc/codeowners-plus (a GitHub Action replacement engine). GitHub's own web UI flags syntax errors but does not simulate a changed-file list against the rules. No free signup-free web page occupies the slot. Structural edge: free vs install-a-toolchain, paste vs checkout, whole file-list vs one path, explains the precedence decision, and runs entirely client-side so a private ownership map never leaves the browser.
ships.borrowed_from: hmarr/codeowners (MIT, Copyright (c) 2020 Harry Marr), pinned at commit 11d3ff2659b769bcb43ddef81a6ab19d1205d9c2 — parse.go's rule/owner state machine and match.go's buildPatternRegex segment rules ported line-for-line. Execution deliberately NOT ported: hmarr is linear-time only because Go's regexp is RE2, and a verbatim JS port into a backtracking RegExp would have reintroduced ship 002's ReDoS. Semantics ported, execution replaced with the lib/nfa.js Pike VM.
ships.checker_verdict:
NOT A PASS. Three independent checkers, none given a prior verdict, all on a DIFFERENT MODEL from the maker. One fix cycle was taken (the contract's maximum) and a fresh adversary re-checked the diff; its verdict is PARTIAL, so this ship is NOT staged and must not be presented as verified.

ROUND 1, primary checker, VERBATIM: "VERDICT: PARTIAL - live-URL unverified (egress). The page's central claim - 'For every file you get the rule that won, the owners GitHub would request' - is false for a real, reproducible input class. lib/codeowners.js's segOne() compiles ? to 'exactly one byte that isn't /', but the reference (hmarr/codeowners match.go) compiles it to 'exactly one Go rune'... CODEOWNERS rule `docs/report-v?.md @docs-team` against changed file `docs/report-va(alpha).md` renders 'no rule matches' / '(none)'... while the real hmarr/codeowners binary says the rule wins... This is a third, undisclosed divergence from the reference." It ran 153 published-oracle pairs (0 mismatches), 27,534 generated adversarial pairs (147 mismatches, 100% containing ?, 0% elsewhere), 2,280 full-file resolve comparisons, 7,411 also-matched membership checks, 33 XSS injections (0 executions), and confirmed the GitHub-docs premise with 0 discrepancies, build reproducibility, ledger/SHIPPED/push consistency, secrets scan, mobile and empty states all clean.

ROUND 1, independent security adversary, VERBATIM: "VERDICT: FAIL. The page's central robustness claim - 'Work is also metered: past the ceiling this page says it cannot evaluate rather than freezing or guessing' - is false. Pasting (verified via real clipboard paste) a single valid CODEOWNERS line consisting of 1,048,536 literal `a` characters... into #owners... freezes the tab for 2,029.9-3,893.7 ms, proven three independent ways... Root cause: co.parseFile (index.html:819) runs to completion - including newPattern->buildPatternAst->nfa.compile/emit, none of which accept a budget - before nfa.makeBudget() is even instantiated at line 837, so compilation is structurally unmeterable today." It also measured the budget ceiling miscalibrated (~4-5M steps/s in Chromium vs the ~40M/s the code assumed). Everything else held: 96 XSS payload x position cases + real-paste (0 dialogs, 0 injected elements; zero `throw` in either module, so the thrown-Error sink that bit ship 002 is structurally impossible here), no prototype pollution, all four limits off-by-one exact both ways, 20,096 budget-vs-unlimited comparisons with 0 wrong answers, 0 cookies/storage and no unexpected egress.

FIX CYCLE (one, as the contract allows). (1) ? now compiles to a 4-branch UTF-8 alternation - one RUNE, not one byte - via new alt()/byteSet() primitives in lib/nfa.js. The root cause is worth more than the fix: the byte/rune equivalence that makes a byte-stepping NFA valid holds for REPEATED constructs and NOT for a single occurrence, so every ASCII test passed. (2) Parsing, AST building and NFA emission are all charged against the budget now, the budget is created BEFORE parsing, and it carries a WALL-CLOCK deadline (750 ms) as well as a step counter - because measured step throughput varies about 7x by workload shape (~32M/s, ~20M/s, ~4-5M/s), so a step budget is not a time bound. 750 ms was chosen from measurement: 1,000 changed files against 200 rules costs ~252 ms.

TARGETED RE-CHECK by a fresh adversary on the fix diff, VERBATIM: "VERDICT: PARTIAL. Defect A (the ? byte-vs-rune bug) is fixed cleanly and completely: 141,583 differential (pattern, path) pairs run against the real Go hmarr/codeowners reference... produced zero mismatches, and 107 direct NFA-level alt() assertions... plus a byte-exact audit of segOne()'s four UTF-8 masks against the Unicode standard... all passed; segOne() is confirmed the only single-occurrence byte matcher in lib/codeowners.js. Defect B (unmetered parse/compile) is only partially fixed: the original catastrophic case (a single ~1 MiB pattern, ~3,894 ms) is genuinely bounded now, but I found and reproduced 13-of-14 times in real Chromium... a block of 1,101-1,291 ms - meaningfully beyond both the page's own '~750 ms' claim and the task's '~1 s' falsification line - from an input that respects every stated limit... Root cause: lib/codeowners.js's runes() (called from both parseRule() and buildPatternAst()) takes no budget parameter and is entirely unmetered, and lib/nfa.js's addThread() has no internal tick()/deadline check inside its while loop... Critically, the safety property still held in every one of these overshoot cases - the page always rendered the correct 'Cannot evaluate' refusal banner, never a partial or wrong table - so this is a timing-claim defect, not a correctness regression." It also flagged LOW: the lib/nfa.js comment's ~252 ms and the page's 'about a quarter of 750 ms' (=187.5 ms) disagree with each other, though its own in-browser measurement (160-198 ms over 6 trials) matches the PAGE's number, so the public claim is not falsified.

WHY THIS IS NOT STAGED: the contract allows exactly ONE fix cycle, and it was spent. Changing code again after the verdict would mean staging something unverified, and the maker never overrides a checker. The remaining defect is a printed number being optimistic by roughly 1.7x on a crafted input - real, and small, and NOT mine to wave through.

VERIFIED SOUND ACROSS THE ROUND (recorded because it is what a rebuild inherits): 141,583 + ~168,000 differential (pattern, path) pairs against independently built Go/RE2 reference binaries with ZERO divergences; 171/171 on the reference implementation's own corpus; 13/13 on GitHub's published example block with the documentation's expectation quoted; 300 randomly generated multi-rule files (7,210 rule lines, 3,933 paths) end-to-end against the reference's own last-match-wins for both winner and skip-set, 0 mismatches, plus CRLF/bare-CR (450 files) and tab-separator cases; ~10,300 constrained-budget comparisons proving the budget only ever refuses and never flips an answer; ~130 XSS payload-positions across three checkers with 0 injections and 0 dialogs (neither module contains a `throw`, so ship 002's thrown-Error sink cannot exist here); 0 prototype pollution; all four input limits off-by-one exact in both directions; 0 cookies, 0 localStorage/sessionStorage, exactly one external request (the cookieless Cloudflare beacon); mobile 390px with 0 horizontal overflow; build reproducibility proven (lib/inline.js regenerates index.html byte for byte, inlined modules identical to lib/); push landed (remote head = local); no secrets or PII in the branch diff. Live-URL unverified by this run (egress); see health.json - which does not exist, because .github/workflows/ has still not been added to the repo.

plain.what: A free web page: paste your CODEOWNERS file and the files a pull request touches, and it tells you exactly who GitHub will ask to review each one — and which of your rules it is quietly ignoring.
plain.solves: CODEOWNERS decides reviewers on every PR, but the LAST matching rule wins, not the most specific one — so teams routinely believe a rule is protecting a directory when a broader rule further down has been overriding it for months. Bad lines are skipped silently, with no warning anywhere.
plain.money: Not published. The build works and is heavily verified, but the independent re-check returned PARTIAL on a timing claim the page prints, so it did not earn a stage. It re-enters tomorrow as a cheap rebuild with the checker's constraint as its build order.

ships.residual_defect: Worst measured main-thread block 1,101-1,291 ms (13 of 14 real-Chromium trials, one outlier at 752 ms) against a page that advertises ~750 ms. Reproduce: CODEOWNERS = 'x'*300000 + ' @o1\n' + '/'.join(['**']*150000) + ' @o2', file list = '/'*4096. Fix is well-scoped and one file deep: give runes() a budget parameter (it is called from parseRule and buildPatternAst and is entirely unmetered) and add a tick() check inside addThread()'s while loop in lib/nfa.js. Down from 3,894 ms before the fix cycle; never yields a wrong answer, only an honest refusal arriving late.
